newsitem.title: FRANCE: French anti-racism group to sue far-right leader.
newsitem.headline: French anti-racism group to sue far-right leader.

text.p: A French anti-racism group said on Tuesday it was taking legal action against a leader of the far-right National Front party for saying that immigrants "pollute our national identity".

The League against Racism and Anti-Semitism (LICRA) said it was filing suit for racial defamation against Bruno Megret, whose wife Catherine became the Front's fourth town mayor last month by winning municipal elections in Vitrolles, southern France.

LICRA said the New York Times had quoted Bruno Megret, the deputy to Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen, as saying that the Front wanted to send Arabs, Africans and Asians home "because they pollute our national identity and take our jobs".
"These views...are unacceptable and unworthy of a responsible politician," LICRA said in a statement. "LICRA has therefore decided to file a complaint...for racial defamation," it said.
In the interview with the New York Times, published on February 12, Megret also called for a tax on companies that employ foreign workers to force them out of their jobs.

Le Pen and Megret have both openly espoused a theory of racial inequality, prompting outrage from anti-racist groups. The centre-right government has said Le Pen's comments were too vague to take him to court for violating laws against inciting racial hatred.
Megret says he is his wife's chief adviser -- he was banned from running for exceeding campaign spending limits in a 1995 poll in Vitrolles.
